info.description:
Multi-tenant backend for Saudi fire-safety and engineering-contracting companies.
**You are reading the `Staging` environment.**

### Start here

1. `POST /api/v1/auth/login` — copy `data.accessToken` from the response.
2. Press **Authorize** above, paste it, and every endpoint below becomes callable.
3. The token carries the company. You do not send a tenant id anywhere.

### Every response has the same shape

```json
{ "isSuccess": true, "message": "…", "data": { }, "errors": null }
```

Read `isSuccess`, not the presence of `data` — `data` is absent on a failure that
carries no payload, and it is legitimately `0`, `false` or `[]` on success. On a
failure, `errors` is an array of sentences already translated into the request's
language and safe to show a user as-is.

### Three headers

| Header | When |
|---|---|
| `Authorization: Bearer …` | Every endpoint except the 20 listed without a padlock. |
| `Accept-Language: ar` or `en` | Always. Arabic is the default, and it is what the user sees if you forget. |
| `X-Tenant-Domain: <subdomain>` | **Anonymous calls only**, to scope them to one company — public branding, subdomain availability. Signed-in calls take the company from the token and ignore this header entirely. |

### Things that surprise people

* **Enums are integers on the wire.** Each one lists its values and their names in the
  schema below, so `role: 202` reads as `ConsultingEngineer` without leaving this page.
* **`402` means the company's subscription has lapsed.** Every write is refused; reads,
  exports and sign-in keep working. A company with no plan is never metered.
* **`403` is a bug in the caller**, not a state to handle: it means a control was
  offered that the user's permissions never allowed. Gate on
  `GET /api/v1/auth/permissions/me`, which returns the effective set as flat strings.
* **`404` covers "not yours" as well as "not there"**, deliberately — a `403` would
  confirm the row exists in another company.
* **Money is computed server-side.** VAT comes from each company's financial policy,
  never a constant.

### Rate limits

Partitioned per company for a signed-in caller and per address otherwise. `429` carries
`Retry-After`; honour it rather than retrying immediately.

### Signing in on this environment

Nine demo accounts exist per company at `{role}@{subdomain}.com` — `admin`,
`deputy`, `engineer`, `operations`, `worker`, `maintenance`, `technician`, `sales`,
`client` — all with the password `User@123456`. `al-salamah` is the company every
example uses.

Three affordances are on here and refused in production: the one-time code comes
back as `data.devOnlyOtp`, the staff invitation token as
`data.devOnlyInvitationToken`, and the payment gateway is bypassed. Build the real
path beside anything that reads them — in production those fields are absent.

get.description:
Takes the same filters as the list, because an export that quietly applies different
rules than the screen it was launched from is worse than no export at all: the discrepancy
surfaces in front of whoever asked for the file.

Capped at 50,000 rows. The X-Export-Truncated response header says so when the
cap was reached, so a narrower date range can be requested rather than a short file being
mistaken for a complete one.

Returns a file rather than the usual ApiResponse<T> envelope, the same
exception FilesController makes: a browser download needs the bytes and a filename,
and base64 inside an envelope would only mean the frontend re-implements the download.

post.summary: Seals the project permanently (FR-CLS-03/04).
post.description:
The point of no return, executed as one transaction. It stamps the final net margin
immutably, compiles the master archive — an indexed manifest of every task, photo verdict,
expense and signature the project produced — converts equipment the project funded into
company-owned assets so no later job is charged for it again (FR-FIN-04), and sets the
write-lock.

Afterwards every record of the job is refused at the database boundary by a
SaveChanges interceptor, not merely by handler checks — so the guarantee holds for
code that has not been written yet.

get.summary: Liveness: is this process running? Checks nothing else, deliberately.
get.description:
An orchestrator uses this to decide whether to restart the container, so it
must not depend on anything outside the process. A liveness probe that touches the database
turns a ten-second database blip into a restart — and because every instance shares that
database, into a restart of every instance at once, which is how a brief outage becomes a
long one.

Answering at all is the signal. There is no unhealthy response: if the process cannot
answer, the probe times out, which is the failure.

get.summary: Readiness: can this instance serve traffic right now?
get.description:
Runs the checks tagged ready — currently the database. An orchestrator uses
this to decide whether to send traffic, so a failure here drains the instance rather
than restarting it, which is the correct response to a dependency being briefly away.

Also the right probe to poll during a deploy: an instance that is alive but still
running migrations is not ready, and sending it traffic produces errors that look like a
bad release.

Not the client's blueprints. Those arrive at intake and hang off the request.
This is the engineer's own output \u2014 a stamped drawing, a hydraulic calculation sheet, a
deficiency report \u2014 the evidence behind a verdict, which until now had nowhere to live.

Accepted only while the job is under engineering review (409 otherwise). The
attachment is claimed by the verdict recorded at the end of the review, and a job that has
moved on has no open verdict to claim it; a later upload would become an orphan that no
engineering record accounts for.

declared content type, and the tenant's storage allowance is checked before anything is
written.

AcceptPlatformInvitationCommand.description:
Accepts a pending platform staff invitation, activating the account and issuing
an authenticated JWT session. The invitee provides:
- UserId: disambiguates which user record to look up (avoids full-table scan)
- InvitationToken: the raw cryptographic token echoed in DevOnlyInvitationToken during Development
- NewPassword / ConfirmPassword: the credentials the invitee chooses for their account

AcceptTenantInvitationCommand.description:
Accepts a pending tenant staff invitation, activating the account and issuing an authenticated
JWT session within the correct tenant boundary. The invitee provides:
- UserId: identifies the pending account (avoids full-table scan)
- InvitationToken: the raw cryptographic token from DevOnlyInvitationToken in Development mode
- NewPassword / ConfirmPassword: credentials chosen by the invitee
An additional guard verifies the target tenant is still active before accepting the invitation.

RegisterClientCommand.description:

The target tenant is resolved automatically from the X-Tenant-Domain header via ICurrentTenantService —

Bearer.description:
Paste the `data.token` value from POST /api/v1/auth/login. Scalar sends it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every request below.

The token carries the company, so once signed in the `X-Tenant-Domain` header is ignored — it is only for anonymous calls that must be scoped to a company.

Demo accounts on Development and Staging, one per role, at `{role}@al-salamah.com` with password `User@123456`: admin, deputy, engineer, operations, worker, maintenance, technician, sales, client.
